verdict.rationale: Stagehand's act() drives pages with plain-English instructions instead of selectors, and observe() returns structured actions to validate before acting. Its accessibility-tree page understanding handles iframes and shadow DOM, and the selfHeal option re-infers an action when its recorded selector breaks. A community comment describes Stagehand as self-healing and more resilient to DOM changes than hardcoded Playwright selectors, which supports the claim of surviving site changes. missing for 10: independent hands-on evidence that actions survive real layout and selector changes (the supporting HN comment appears vendor-adjacent), and explicit documentation of separate click/type primitives on described elements beyond act().
